outroLine: How many did you get? Comment your score below, and subscribe with the bell on for a new quiz every day!

lines.q: Thirty capital cities, from easy to legend, and they get harder every round. Keep score! First one: What is the capital of the United Kingdom?
lines.a: London! Home of the world's very first underground railway.

lines.q: What is the capital of China?
lines.a: Beijing! Shanghai is bigger, but Beijing runs the show.

lines.q: What is the capital of Mexico?
lines.a: Mexico City! Built on an old lake, more than two thousand metres up.

lines.q: What is the capital of Austria?
lines.a: Vienna! Mozart and Beethoven both made music there.

lines.q: What is the capital of Sweden?
lines.a: Stockholm! A capital spread across fourteen islands.

lines.q: Last one of round one. What is the capital of Thailand?
lines.a: Bangkok! Its full ceremonial name is one of the longest on Earth.

lines.q: Round two: medium, and the traps begin. What is the capital of India?
lines.a: New Delhi! Not Mumbai, the trap most people fall into.

lines.q: What is the capital of the Netherlands?
lines.a: Amsterdam! The government sits in The Hague, but the capital is Amsterdam.

lines.q: What is the capital of Poland?
lines.a: Warsaw! Kraków was the old royal capital until around sixteen hundred.

lines.q: What is the capital of Peru?
lines.a: Lima! Cusco was the Inca capital, Lima came with the Spanish.

lines.q: What is the capital of the Philippines?
lines.a: Manila! Quezon City actually held the title from nineteen forty eight to seventy six.

lines.q: What is the capital of Cuba?
lines.a: Havana! Famous for its classic old cars.

lines.q: Round three: hard. Stay sharp! What is the capital of Saudi Arabia?
lines.a: Riyadh! Its name means the gardens.

lines.q: What is the capital of the United Arab Emirates?
lines.a: Abu Dhabi! Dubai is more famous, but it is not the capital.

lines.q: What is the capital of Colombia?
lines.a: Bogotá! Over two and a half kilometres up in the Andes. If you're enjoying this, subscribe and turn on the bell!

lines.q: What is the capital of Chile?
lines.a: Santiago! Fun twist: Chile's congress meets in Valparaíso. Great going so far!

lines.q: What is the capital of Hungary?
lines.a: Budapest! Three towns, Buda, Óbuda and Pest, merged into one.

lines.q: What is the capital of Ecuador?
lines.a: Quito! Guayaquil is bigger, but Quito is the capital.

lines.q: Round four: very hard. Only the best get these. What is the capital of Cameroon?
lines.a: Yaoundé! Douala is bigger, but Yaoundé is the capital.

lines.q: What is the capital of Belize?
lines.a: Belmopan! Built inland after a hurricane battered Belize City.

lines.q: What is the capital of Slovenia?
lines.a: Ljubljana! Its symbol is a dragon. Bratislava is Slovakia, by the way.

lines.q: What is the capital of Uruguay?
lines.a: Nice one if you got it! Montevideo! It hosted the very first World Cup final.

lines.q: What is the capital of Paraguay?
lines.a: Asunción! One of the oldest cities in South America.

lines.q: What is the capital of Malta?
lines.a: Valletta! The smallest capital in the whole European Union.

lines.q: Final round: legend level! What is the capital of Liechtenstein?
lines.a: Vaduz! A capital with fewer than ten thousand people.

lines.q: What is the capital of Kyrgyzstan?
lines.a: Bishkek! In Soviet times it was called Frunze.

lines.q: What is the capital of Laos?
lines.a: Vientiane! Luang Prabang was the old royal capital.

lines.q: Three left, stay with me! What is the capital of Suriname?
lines.a: Paramaribo! And fun fact, people there speak Dutch.

lines.q: What is the capital of Brunei?
lines.a: Bandar Seri Begawan! Famous for a whole village on stilts.

lines.q: Final question. What is the capital of Palau?
lines.a: Ngerulmud! Palau moved its capital there from Koror in two thousand six.

questions.q: What is the capital of **United Kingdom**?
questions.fact: The London Underground opened in 1863 – the world's first.
The Forbidden City has around 980 buildings.
Mexico City sits about 2,240 m above sea level.
Mozart, Haydn and Beethoven all worked in Vienna.
Stockholm is spread across 14 islands.
Bangkok's ceremonial name is one of the longest place names on Earth.
New Delhi was inaugurated as the capital in 1931.
The government sits in The Hague, but the capital is Amsterdam.
The royal court moved from Kraków to Warsaw around 1600.
Lima was founded by Francisco Pizarro in 1535.
Quezon City was the capital from 1948 to 1976.
Old Havana became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1982.

questions.q: What is the capital of **Saudi Arabia**?
questions.fact: Riyadh means 'the gardens' in Arabic.

questions.q: What is the capital of **United Arab Emirates**?
questions.fact: Abu Dhabi is by far the largest of the seven emirates.
Bogotá sits about 2,600 m up in the Andes.
Chile's Congress meets in Valparaíso, not Santiago.
Budapest was formed in 1873 by joining Buda, Óbuda and Pest.
Quito was among the first UNESCO World Heritage Sites in 1978.
Douala is the biggest city, but Yaoundé is the capital.
Belmopan was built after Hurricane Hattie hit Belize City in 1961.
Ljubljana's symbol is a dragon – see the Dragon Bridge.
Montevideo hosted the first World Cup final in 1930.
Founded in 1537, Asunción is one of South America's oldest cities.
Valletta is the smallest capital city in the EU.
Vaduz has fewer than 10,000 residents.
Bishkek was called Frunze in Soviet times.
Luang Prabang was the old royal capital of Laos.
Suriname's official language is Dutch.
Its water village, Kampong Ayer, is built on stilts.
Palau moved its capital from Koror to Ngerulmud in 2006.
